title: When People Got Sick: Salmonella Outbreaks, April 2026 | Salmonella Infection | CDC
content: When People Got Sick: Salmonella Outbreaks, April 2026 For Everyone May 14, 2026 Key points Public health officials in several states are investigating three multistate outbreaks of Salmonella illnesses linked to contact with backyard poultry. Over a quarter of the sick people in these outbreaks are children under 5 years old. The largest outbreak has an unusually high number of people reporting contact with ducks. Any backyard poultry can carry Salmonella germs that can make you sick. Always take steps to stay healthy around your flock. When people got sick This chart shows when the 184 people in these Salmonella outbreaks got sick. Recent illnesses may not yet be reported as it usually takes 3 to 4 weeks to determine if a sick person is part of an outbreak. The true number of sick people in this outbreak is also likely much higher than the number reported. This is because many people recover without medical care and are not tested for Salmonella .
